name: claude-code-design-transfer-registry
purpose: Records which publicly documented Claude Code design patterns are useful to transfer into the platform-first desktop app without depending on leaked, private, or unverifiable material.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry when improving the installable platform with ideas inspired by Claude Code. It is a source-boundary and implementation map, not a clone plan.
how_to_read: Read source_boundary first; only public official or otherwise verifiable sources can justify a transfer pattern.
Read transfer_patterns to see the reusable design principle, current platform mapping, risk controls, and implementation target.
Treat status as product planning state: implemented means surfaced now, queued means designed but not fully built, candidate means useful but not committed.
Use risk_controls before turning a pattern into autonomous execution, installer behavior, hooks, or connector access.
update_triggers: Official Claude Code documentation changes a relevant design surface.
The platform adds a new desktop runtime, CLI adapter, hook, connector, subagent, skill, or memory feature.
A transfer pattern becomes executable rather than documentation-only.
A source is discovered to be non-public, unverified, or incompatible with the platform source boundary.
Workspace Monitor needs a new operator-facing view of design transfer status.

structure_rules.rule: No transfer pattern may cite leaked, proprietary, private, or unverifiable material as a design basis.
structure_rules.reason: The platform must improve from public evidence and local validation, not confidential material.

structure_rules.rule: Claude Code CLI can be an optional guest adapter or design reference, but the desktop app remains the primary platform host runtime.
structure_rules.reason: The product owns task state, decisions, memory, artifacts, validation, and UI authority.

structure_rules.rule: Instruction memory can guide behavior, but permissions, sensitive boundaries, and destructive operations require enforced settings or user decisions.
structure_rules.reason: Official Claude Code docs distinguish contextual instructions from enforced client policy; the platform should keep the same separation.

structure_rules.rule: Promote a repeated workflow into the smallest useful asset before making it a platform feature.
structure_rules.reason: Skills, prompts, workflows, templates, tools, agents, and product features have different maintenance costs.

field_guide.meaning: The explicit rule that only public, official, or otherwise verifiable sources may drive design transfer.
Reusable Claude Code-inspired design patterns mapped to this platform's existing and planned assets.
Reference link IDs that support the pattern. These are verification handles, not automatic proof.
The publicly documented Claude Code behavior or architecture signal being adapted.
How the pattern should appear in the platform-first desktop app or adjacent platform project.
Controls needed before the pattern can affect files, tools, secrets, processes, connectors, hooks, or public claims.

source_boundary.public_decision: If an idea is only known through leaked or non-public material, do not use it. Re-derive a safe pattern from official docs or local platform needs instead.

transfer_patterns.label: Permissioned Tool Execution
transfer_patterns.claude_code_signal: Settings and permissions have scopes and precedence, while CLAUDE.md-style instructions are contextual guidance rather than hard enforcement.
transfer_patterns.transfer_principle: Separate behavioral guidance from enforced execution policy.
transfer_patterns.platform_mapping: Keep CLI adapters optional, use allowlisted Tauri commands, persist human decisions, and route unsafe source-affecting choices through the decision inbox.
implementation_targets: Show permission and source-boundary status in Workspace Monitor
Add per-adapter permission summaries before source-affecting task pipes
risk_controls: no global CLI install without audit
explicit human checkpoint for destructive operations

transfer_patterns.label: Plan Before Edit
transfer_patterns.claude_code_signal: Plan mode reads files and proposes a plan before disk edits for changes that need review.
transfer_patterns.transfer_principle: Use reversible planning gates before durable source or policy edits.
transfer_patterns.platform_mapping: Map plan mode to work modes, spec-driven tasks, task pipe merge gates, and decision inbox checkpoints.
implementation_targets: Add a first-class Plan Gate indicator to Desktop task pipes
Show blocked decisions next to the source editor before Save All
risk_controls: mode selection record for non-quick work

transfer_patterns.label: Durable Instruction Memory
transfer_patterns.claude_code_signal: CLAUDE.md and auto memory are loaded into sessions, but enforcement belongs in settings or hooks.
transfer_patterns.transfer_principle: Keep shared durable instructions thin, traceable, and separate from hard policy.
transfer_patterns.platform_mapping: Use AGENTS.md as a runtime adapter entrypoint and keep durable policy in shared docs/configs with memory bootstrap anchors.
implementation_targets: Show memory bootstrap hot anchors in Workspace Monitor
Flag adapter instructions that duplicate durable policy
risk_controls: do not fork durable policy across adapters
specific concise instructions over vague preferences

transfer_patterns.label: Subagent Context Isolation
transfer_patterns.claude_code_signal: Subagents preserve main context by handling side tasks in separate contexts with scoped tool access.
transfer_patterns.transfer_principle: Treat exploration, research, validation, implementation, and merge gates as separate lanes with explicit summaries.
transfer_patterns.platform_mapping: Expose agent collaboration lanes, task pipe presets, blockers, and merge gates rather than dumping every log into the main task view.
implementation_targets: Add per-lane context budget and summary contracts
Surface lane handoff quality in Unified Ops
risk_controls: parallel lanes need non-overlapping touch paths

transfer_patterns.label: MCP Connector Boundary
transfer_patterns.claude_code_signal: MCP connects external tools and data sources, but trust and prompt-injection risks must be reviewed before connecting servers.
transfer_patterns.transfer_principle: Connectors are optional capability cards with trust, scope, and lifecycle checks.
transfer_patterns.platform_mapping: Keep MCP-style connectors behind capability setup, permission review, and source-boundary warnings rather than making them required platform runtime dependencies.
implementation_targets: Add connector cards next to CLI adapter cards
Record connector trust decisions in the decision inbox

transfer_patterns.label: Hook Event Automation
transfer_patterns.claude_code_signal: Hooks can run commands around tool and session events, and command hooks run with the user's permissions.
transfer_patterns.transfer_principle: Automation hooks need explicit event schemas, allowlists, rollback, and resource guards.
transfer_patterns.platform_mapping: Use hook-like workflows only after modeling event input/output, cleanup, and user permission impact.
implementation_targets: Create a platform hook registry with disabled-by-default executable hooks
Show hook risk state in Desktop Capability Center

transfer_patterns.label: Skill On-Demand Packaging
transfer_patterns.claude_code_signal: Skills package repeatable workflows and load detailed instructions only when relevant.
transfer_patterns.transfer_principle: Promote repeated work into the smallest durable capability before adding product code.
transfer_patterns.platform_mapping: Use templates, tools, skills, prompts, workflows, and agents as staged capability assets; surface promotion candidates in evidence/promotion views.
implementation_targets: Show skill candidates from work history bottlenecks
Link skill validation results into Workspace Monitor
risk_controls: forward-test before relying on a skill

transfer_patterns.label: Parallel Worktree Sessions
transfer_patterns.claude_code_signal: Parallel sessions can run in separate worktrees to reduce edit collisions.
transfer_patterns.transfer_principle: Parallel execution requires branch/worktree isolation or explicit touch-path locks.
transfer_patterns.platform_mapping: Task pipes should record lane touch paths, dependencies, and merge strategy before launching overlapping implementation work.
implementation_targets: Add worktree-aware task pipe launch options
Show touch-path conflict warnings before multi-lane source edits
risk_controls: no overlapping write paths without lock or handoff
